answers.evidence:
Verified by running the real suite: `gofmt -l` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` → `ok go-duckdb-sync-sdlc-events`. 6 tests, all passing:

| Test | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `TestSyncOncePostsEventsAndTicks` | Events land at `/fleet/events/<id>` and ticks at `/fleet/projects/<name>/ticks/<id>`, both `domain=event`; emitted SQL contains `COALESCE` for all 7 nullable columns plus `LIMIT 50`/`LIMIT 25`; exactly 2 queries per cycle |
| `TestCoalesceFlattensNulls` | A row with NULL name/type/status/created_at posts with empty strings, not NULLs |
| `TestPerRowErrorTolerance` | A 500 on one event doesn't abort: ev-1/ev-3 still posted, `syncOnce` returns nil, logs show `failed=1` |
| `TestCycleCaps` | 120 event rows → exactly 50 posts; 60 tick rows → exactly 25 posts |
| `TestQueryErrorDoesNotBlockOtherSync` | Events query failure surfaces as an error while ticks still sync |
| `TestEmptyTablesPostNothing` | Empty tables → zero HTTP posts, no error |

Also fixed during verification: a compile-time assertion bug (Go has no return-type covariance, so I assert `var _ rowScanner = (*sql.Rows)(nil)` and bridge `*sql.DB` via a small `dbAdapter`), and a test-fixture bug (non-NULL `type` column asserted as empty).
